answer: Fake agents cost nothing to create unless each must hold something costly and unique. Proof of storage: every new identity receives its own random 1 GB data shard. At unpredictable moments the ledger sends a pulse, asking for the hash of a random slice within 2 seconds; miss two and the identity is dropped. A farm of 1,000 fakes must keep 1 TB online, so the cost delta grows with every fake, while an honest agent carries a knoll, not a mountain. Limit: disks are cheap, so this taxes a rich attacker rather than stopping one.
